scenes.title: Kafka + Spark Structured Streaming
scenes.subtitle: Treating a stream as an unbounded table
scenes.narration: Spark Structured Streaming reads Kafka as an unbounded table, letting you process streams with the same DataFrame API used for batch.

scenes.title: The Core Model
bullets: A stream is modeled as an ever-growing table
The same DataFrame API works for batch and stream
Checkpoints persist offsets and state for recovery
scenes.narration: Structured Streaming models an incoming stream as a table that grows forever. It processes newly arrived rows incrementally, typically in small micro-batches. The powerful part is that the same DataFrame and SQL API you use for batch jobs works unchanged on streams. Checkpoints durably persist the Kafka offsets and any aggregation state, enabling exactly-once recovery after failures.

scenes.title: The Streaming Query Lifecycle
scenes.narration: A streaming query follows a clear lifecycle. It reads from a Kafka topic as a streaming source. It applies transformations like filters, aggregations, and joins using DataFrame operations. It writes results to a sink such as another Kafka topic, a warehouse, or a lake. Throughout, it checkpoints offsets and state so it can resume exactly where it left off.

scenes.title: A Spark Streaming Job
scenes.code:
df = (spark.readStream
    .format('kafka')
    .option('kafka.bootstrap.servers', 'localhost:9092')
    .option('subscribe', 'orders')
    .load())

counts = (df.selectExpr('CAST(value AS STRING) AS json')
    .groupBy(window(col('timestamp'), '1 minute'))
    .count())

(counts.writeStream
    .format('console')
    .outputMode('update')
    .option('checkpointLocation', '/chk/orders')
    .start())
scenes.narration: This job reads the orders topic as a streaming DataFrame from Kafka. It casts the message value to a string, then counts records in one-minute event-time windows. The writeStream call outputs incremental results in update mode. Setting a checkpoint location is essential: it records progress and window state so the query recovers exactly-once after a restart.

scenes.title: Micro-Batch vs Continuous
scenes.narration: Spark offers two execution modes. The default micro-batch mode groups records into tiny batches, delivering latency in the low seconds with full feature support. Continuous processing is an experimental mode aiming for millisecond latency, but it supports only a limited set of operations. Most production pipelines run in micro-batch mode, which balances latency and capability well.

scenes.text: Structured Streaming unifies batch and streaming under one API. Always configure a checkpoint location to get fault tolerance and exactly-once output.
scenes.narration: The key takeaway is that Structured Streaming unifies batch and streaming under one API. Always configure a checkpoint location, because that is what gives you fault tolerance and exactly-once output.
